questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The earth's magnetic field was flipped by <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>180</mn><mo>°</mo></math> a million years ago. This flip was relatively rapid and took <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msup><mn>10</mn><mn>5</mn></msup></math> years. Then the average change in orientation per year during the flip closest to
options: <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>1</mn></math> second.
<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>5</mn></math> second.
<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>10</mn></math> second.
<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>30</mn></math> second.
questions.solution:
1°=3600 arc sec

average change in orientation per year =180°105 degree year-1

=180×3600105 sec year-1

=1.8×0.36

=6.48 sec year-1

Closest option (B)

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A charged particle, initially at rest at $\mathrm{O}$, When released follows atrajectory as shown. Such a trajectory is possible in the presence of
options: Electric field of constant magnitude and varying direction
Magnetic field of constant magnitude and varying direction
Electric field of constant magnitude and constant direction
Electric and magnetic fields of constant magnitudes and constant directions which are parallel to each other
questions.solution: In option B it will not move, in option $C \& D$ path will be straight line.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A bar magnet falls with its north pole pointing down through the axis of a copper ring. When viewed from above, the currecnt in the ring will be
options: Clockwise while the magnet is above the plane of the ring and counter clockwise while below the plane of the ring
Counter clockwise throughout
Counter clockwise while the magnet is above the plane of the ring, and clockwise while below the plane of the ring
Clockwise throughout.
questions.solution: Useing lenz's law upper face first become North pole then south pole

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q:
An arangement with a pair of quarter circular coils of radii $r$ and $R$ with a common centre $C$ and carrying a current $I$ is shown.
The permeability of free space is $\mu_{0}$. The magnetic field at $C$ is
options: $\mu_{0} \mid(1 / r-1 / R) / 8$ into the page
$\mu_{0} \mid(1 / r+1 / R) / 8$ out of the page
$\mu_{0} \mid(1 / r-1 / R) / 8$ out of the page
$\mu_{0} \mid(1 / r+1 / R) / 8$ into the page
questions.solution: $B$ due to Arc $=\frac{\mu_{0} i \theta}{4 \pi r}\frac{\mu_{0} i}{8}\left[\frac{1}{r}-\frac{1}{R}\right]$ out of the page

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A metallic ring of radius a and resistance $R$ is held fixed with its axis along a spatially uniform magnetic field whose magnitude is $\mathrm{B}_{0} \sin (\omega \mathrm{t})$. Neglect gravity. Then;
options: the current in the ring oscillates with a frequency of $2 \omega$
the joule heating loss in the ring is proportional to $\mathrm{a}^{2}$
the force per unit length on the ring will be proportional to $B_{0}^{2}$
the net force on the ring is non-zero
questions.solution:
\frac{d F}{d L}=\frac{B}{R}\left(\frac{d B \cdot A}{d t}\right)

Where $\mathrm{B}=\mathrm{B}_{0} \sin \omega t$
